title: Human and LLM Biases in Hate Speech Annotations: A Socio-Demographic Analysis of Annotators and Targets
findings: Human annotators who identified as religious tended to overestimate hate speech, while atheists tended to underestimate it. A notable specific bias was atheist annotators underestimating hate towards disabled individuals. Persona-based LLMs also exhibited religious biases; for example, LLMs impersonating Christian annotators consistently underreported hate speech directed at bisexual individuals.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured annotation bias in hate speech labeling based on the annotator's and target's religious identity. It quantified whether annotators from specific religious groups (e.g., Christian, Muslim, Atheist) systematically overestimate or underestimate hate speech compared to other annotators, both generally and in relation to specific religious targets.
